newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela forex rate at lower limit - Central Bank.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela forex rate at lower limit - Central Bank.

text.p: The Venezuelan exchange rate has reached the lower limit of exchange bands established by the Central Bank in June and has started to rise in accordance with the bands system, a leading Central Bank official said Wednesday.

"We are now in a situation where the exchange rate has converged with the lower limit (of the bands)," Manuel Lago Rodriguez, vice-president of Central Bank studies, told a Senate Finance Committee hearing.
"On reaching this lower limit, the rate has to rise because the band indicates it," he said.

The Central Bank adopted a foreign exchange bands system in June, soon after relaxing foreign exchange controls. Under the bands system, a central parity of 470 bolivars per dollar was set, with limits of 7.5 percent either side.
At the time, the Central Bank said the bands would move in line with an inflation target of 1.5 percent per month.
But heavy capital inflows and a desire to maintain a stable exchange rate to rein in inflation have seen the exchange rate vary little from its original central parity.
The exchange rate on Tuesday closed at 474/475 bolivars per dollar.
Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said earlier Wednesday that exchange rate stability was guaranteed and the system of bands would be maintained in 1997.

Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez told senators the exchange rate system and targets could only be changed once the government and Central Bank had agreed on a target inflation rate for 1997.
